name: Charleville Forest Yew

official_register.name: Tree Register of Ireland (no. 181) / Heritage Trees of Ireland

access: Charleville Forest woodland is walked without a fee or permit according to Komoot's local Q&A and Visit Offaly, but no operator page states it; the demesne entrance is next to the King Oak. One walker's account says the King Oak is seen from the driveway at the gate, so confirm the forest gate is open on the day. Castle tours are separate and paid.
transport: About 3 km west of Tullamore town centre on the R421 (roughly 5 minutes by car; Tullamore station is the nearest rail stop, 3 km, no direct bus checked)
verify_notes: FLAGGED: register only, one source family. The Ancient Yew Group database record 2731 reproduces the Tree Register of Ireland entry (no. 181): girth 5.62 m in 2009, 12 m high, described by the register as 'a large girthed yew tree on the edge of an oak forest'; Aubrey Fennell recorded 559 cm at 1 m between 2000 and 2005, so the trunk is thickening slowly or measurement noise. Heritage Trees of Ireland record 620 (visited 17 Aug 2009, multi-stem form, band 300-500 years as of 2009) gives grid N311230 = 53.25652,-7.53291, precision 100 m. CONFLICT ON PLACE: the Ancient Yew page puts the same record at 53.26499,-7.51089 (about 1.7 km east, near the King Oak end of the demesne, read from a map link, grid reference 'not known'). The grid-derived point is used here; the other is probably a click on the map. Not alive-checked: lifecheck NONE, no dated photo or news of this tree found. A walker's account mentions a yew planting in a union-flag pattern at Charleville (not placed, not this tree). RECOGNITION CANDIDATE: a very thick multi-stemmed yew standing at the edge of the oak woodland, dark evergreen against deciduous oak; no building or path anchor found in sources. Pin cannot be tied to one crown, so findability depends on a reader or photo. Age is the register band, not derived from girth.
